description: Seven mathematicians at one table, each a neuron and each a voice, answering about the Riemann hypothesis with a model's words. Every character stands where the file puts it - x along the ground, z into the picture, so a near one is larger and a far one smaller - and every character answers with its own hand. The run is the conversation: the cue asks, Ada answers, and each answer goes to the next in the arc until the last is turned away at maxHops.

neurons.description: The question the table is asked: whoever holds the stage says it once and the room hears it.
Ada, nearest the camera and furthest from certainty: an analytic number theorist who will not take a hunch for evidence.
Rosa, who trusts only counts, and has checked more zeros than anyone at the table and still says it proves nothing.
Bruno, one step back and already certain: he hears the zeros as a chord and overclaims in images.
Iris, further back still: a historian who dates every claim and knows exactly who proved what, and when.
Otto at the back of the room: a physicist who hears random matrices in the zeros and trusts analogy over proof.
Lea, coming round the far side: a formalist who wants to know what 'true' is supposed to mean here.
Jules, plain and impatient: not a number theorist, and not shy about asking what the theorem would pay for.

payload.text: The Riemann hypothesis. Around this table, one line each: is it true, or only very well tested?

data.say: Only tested; ten trillion zeros support it, but belief is not proof.
